text:
Noah Ostlund is the biggest role change on our board. He is playing 18:58 a night, up from 13:58 last season, and he is on the ice for 75 percent of Buffalo's power play after 15 percent a year ago. He has 10 points in 16 games, and his own chances have more than doubled, to 0.98 expected goals per 60 minutes from 0.45.

The skills fit the role. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 67 percent of his shots coming off the rush last season and 20 percent of his setups crossing the royal road, nearly three times a typical forward. Evolving-Hockey liked his defense more than his offense, 91st percentile at suppressing chances. That's a rare thing in a 22-year-old, and it's how a young center earns minutes from a coach.

He is shooting 10 percent, a bit under average, so nothing is inflated. Forwards drafted where he went score a median 0.31 points a game in their first real season; he's at 0.62. Small sample, big minutes, and our range has him around 53 points.
headline: Ostlund has gone from fourth line to a big role
